newsitem.title: USA: Westcoast seen cutting 25 pct McMahon output.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast seen cutting 25 pct McMahon output.

text.p: Westcoast Energy has cut about 25 percent of the natural gas production at its McMahon plant in northeastern British Columbia, traders said.
"They lost 25 percent of production," said one gas trader in western Canada.
The company was not immediately available to confirm the cuts or comment on when the plant was likely to restore full operations.
McMahon, which processes about 700 million cubic feet of gas a day (mmcfd), has had a spate of operational problems over the past few days.

Traders said news of more problems at the plant sent spot prices 10 cents higher into the US$1.20-1.25 per mmBtu range at Sumas, Wash., the main export point for Canadian gas into the U.S. west coast market said.
On Wednesday, the company said it had declared a force majeure due to constraints at its sulfur plant. The force majeure was lifted shortly thereafter.
The plant was also shut for a few hours on Tuesday after mechanical problems occurred in its control system.
McMahon, which is a central collection point for gas pipelines in western Canada, has suffered a series of operational problems over the last several months.
